text:
ConocoPhillips gained 1.67% today, rebounding after a two-week slide that saw the stock drop 7.5%. The bounce likely reflects optimism around oil prices and geopolitical risk: Brent crude briefly dipped below $90 a barrel yesterday on hopes of an Iran conflict resolution, but President Trump signaled the situation may be defusing ("going to be ending fairly soon"), which eases near-term supply concerns that had been weighing on energy stocks.

The broader backdrop matters too. Over the past two weeks, oil price volatility tied to Iran tensions had pressured the stock, but yesterday's remarks suggesting de-escalation may have stabilized that fear. The gap between US crude ($99.64) and Brent ($107.03) remains wide, suggesting international demand or supply concerns persist—so today's gain is modest relief rather than a clear turnaround.
